Q: How do I visit friends' farms?\n\n\nT:
Q: How do I visit friends' farms?


To visit a friend's farm, just tap the social button in the bottom-left corner of your screen, hit their name under "Neighbors", and tap visit.


Q: How do I add friends?


To find friends through Facebook and your phone contacts, tap the social button, tap "Find Neighbors", and hit the Facebook connect button.  Once your Facebook account is linked to Zombie Farm, tap "Players you may know."


You can also manually add players by entering their email addresses or Playforge Usernames into the "Find Players" pane.


Q: How do I play tag?


To play tag, first visit a friend's farm (you should have one friend by default).  Once the farm has loaded, hit the "Play Tag" button on the right-hand side of the screen.


The rules of tag are simple: try to make your farmer hit as many of the zombies as you can within the time limit.  The faster you finish, the better your score!


Q: Do I need to create a Playforge Username to keep playing Zombie Farm?


While it is possible to play Zombie Farm without a Playforge Username, we strongly recommend that you create one.  Doing so will give you access to friends, free gifts, zombie tag, and much more!


Q: What is a Playforge Username?


Your Player Username is your social identity when playing Zombie Farm.  When a player adds you as a friend, your Player Username will appear in their "Neighbors" panel.  In addition, other players can add you as a friend by entering your Player Username into the "Find Players" pane (accessed by clicking "Find Neighbors" under the Neighbors tab).


Q: How do I save my game?


When you tap on the game menu (upper left button) you'll see a Save Game button, tap it to manually save your farm.  Zombie Farm also saves your game automatically whenever you quit the app.  In addition, it's a good idea to perform periodical backups of your device through iTunes.


Q: I just started; can I have more than 6 patches of soil?


Yes!  Select the plow tool (green button), and a square marker will appear on your farm. Drag it to where you want your new patch of soil to be, and then tap to confirm. You will then have a brand new patch of soil to plant on.


Q: How do I move stuff around on my farm?


Everything except for zombies and soil patches can be moved in Zombie Farm.  To move an item, select the move tool (dark blue button), and tap on an object.  Then, using your finger, drag the object around the farm, once you have found a suitable place, let go of the item to place it.


Q: How do I rotate items on my farm?


Select the rotate tool in the tool menu (light blue button). Tap the item you wish to rotate, and it will rotate by ninety degrees.  Keep in mind that while most of the items on your farm can be rotated, objects that cannot be moved cannot be rotated.  In addition, symmetrical items (such as road intersections and balloons) will not appear to change when rotated.


 Q: How do I store an item on my farm?


 When you reach level 8, you can buy your first storage building: the Shabby Shed.  Once you have this building on your farm you can start storing items. To do so, tap an item on your farm, and hit the blue button in the tool tip that appears. An informative window will appear which gives you the option to store the item!


 Q: How do I retrieve an item from storage?


 You can access the storage menu two ways.  The most popular method is to go to the tool menu and tap the "Storage" button on the right panel.  Alternatively, you can tap the storage building itself, and then tap the blue button that appears in its tool tip.


 Q: What do I do with all these zombies on my farm?


 Zombies love to just hang around the farm, but they're also important money makers. You need zombies to perform invasions. If you win an invasion, you are rewarded with a combination of gold, boosts, rare items, and occasionally a brain. You need at least 8 zombies to invade, but will have best results with a full 16.  


 Q: How do I get brains?


 There are three ways to get brains in Zombie Farm:

 1. Purchase them in-game under the market menu. 

 2. Invade.  Winning an invasion will sometimes reward you with a brain in addition to the gold you plunder. 

 3. Spin the "Wheel of Fortune".  This wheel initially gives you a 4% chance of winning a brain, but this chance is raised every day you delay in claiming your prize.  


 Q: What's the deal with my hungry zombies?


 The longer zombies go without invading, the hungrier they get.  Hungry zombies are great to bring to an invasion - the hungrier they are, the more eager they will be to fight! Hungry zombies take less time to deploy during an invasion, and they don't get as distracted as zombies who have just eaten. 


 Q: How do I feed my zombies?


 When zombies participate in an invasion, regardless of the invasion's outcome, they will become well fed after the fight.


 Q: Will zombies die if i don't feed them?


 Zombies can't die since they're already dead!  You can only lose zombies in combat or by selling them.


 Q: How do I fight?


 You are allowed to fight if you have 8 or more zombies, though it's best to fight with a full 16. Once you have enough zombies, an "Invade" button will appear in your Zombie Farm toolbar right above Zombies. You must wait two hours between invasions, unless you purchase an Invasion Voucher under the "Boosts" tab of your Market.  


 Q: What's this window that pops up when I select an enemy to invade?


 Once you hit "Invade", use this window to select the order of your zombies during the invasion..  You can see all of your zombies by sliding the menu to the right.  Tap your zombies in the order that you want them to be deployed.  If you want the game to choose for you, you can hit the "Pick For Me" button.


 Q: Where is the item I won from my invasion? 


 All items that drop from an invasion go straight to your storage. Don't worry about not having enough space or even a storage building, as it'll still go in there.


 Q: I won a rusty fragment.  Where can I find it?


 Rusty fragments can be found in the storage menu.  Once you have a stack of three, tap on it for a special surprise!


 Q: Why do my crops wilt so fast?


 Fast crops like carrots and mini zombies will wilt within an hour of ripening. If you find that your crops are wilting too quickly, try planting crops that take longer to grow.


 Q: How long does it take for a crop to wilt?


 A crop will stay ripe for three times its growth period. For example, tomatoes grow in 4 hours, and wilt twelve hours after ripening.


 Q: Do zombies wilt too?


 They sure do.


 Q: What does fertilizing do?


 Fertilizing doubles the gold value of a crop when harvested. In addition, fertilizing a zombie ensures that it will never be lifeless when you harvest it.  Fertilizing is done automatically by Garden Zombies, Zombotanists, Flower Zombies, and Zombees.  The more of these zombies you have on your farm, the better chances your crops have of being fertilized.


 Q: What is "Life Force"?


 Having a high Life Force lessens the chances you have of harvesting lifeless zombies. Life Force also affects the success of zombie mutations. Trees give the most life force per square tile.


 Q: How do I know how much "Life Force" I have?


 Life force is displayed at the top of your farm, just to the right of your zombie count.


 Q: What are Zombie Mutations?


 Once you have unlocked a mutation from the market menu, try planting a zombie next to the crop whose mutation you purchased. When it's time to harvest the Zombie, you just might end up with a mutant.  So, if you have the Onion mutation unlocked, plant your zombies right next to the onions. It won't matter if the onion isn't fully grown - just remember to harvest the zombie before harvesting the crop.


 Q: What good are Mutant Zombies?


 Besides looking funny, mutants are better in combat than regular zombies. Check the Market for details on each mutation.


 Q: What the heck are Combined Zombies?


 Combined Zombies are the fourth and most powerful form of zombies that can be created; they are made by combining two zombies together in a Zombie Pot (available at lvl 25).  After an hour (or fifteen minutes with a Clay Monolith), these zombies are ready to be taken out.  


 Note: If you combine any two zombies of the same type, the resulting Combined Zombie will always be a more powerful version of that zombie type.  So, combining two Flamehead Zombies will always result in a Party Zombie.  However, if you combine two zombies of different types, the outcome has an even chance of going either way. 


 Q: That sounds great, but how do I actually combine?


 To create Combined Zombies, you must reach level 25, purchase a Zombie Pot from the market, and place it on your farm.  Tap on the pot and you'll be prompted to select 2 zombies on your farm. Once you've selected your zombies, you'll then be asked if you want to combine them. Once you've hit "yes", the combining process begins; this normally takes an hour, but can be shortened to fifteen minutes with a Clay Monolith.


 Q: Does color matter for Combined Zombies?


 No, color doesn't matter, so feel free to come up with any color combination you can think of!


 Q: What happens to mutations when combining?


 If both of the zombies have the same mutation, the combined zombie will have a 100% of getting that mutation.  However, if only one zombie has a mutation, there's a small chance that the combined zombie won't get it.


 Q: How do I see zombie stats?


 To see a zombie's stats, tap on the zombie in question, and press the blue button next to its name. This brings you to the zombie menu, where you can see all of your zombies' stats. Alternatively, you can tap the "Zombies" menu button just below "Invade".  


 Q: What's a zombie veteran?


 Zombies earn veteran rank once they survive an invasion.  Once a zombie has increased its veteran rank four times, it will reach the "master" rank. Each rank gives your zombies a 5% boost to all their stats, so try not to lose any zombies when invading!


 Q: What about that zombie "Ability" tab?


 Every time you win an invasion, you unlock a new zombie ability.  Once unlocked, these show up under the "Ability" tabs for each zombie.  Most abilities are passive, but some (such as the Zombarian abilities "Bash" and "Smash") are activated by tapping them during an invasion.  


 Q: What is a Zombie Patch?


 If you feel your zombies are a bit unruly running about your farm, try using a Zombie Patch. Zombies love to snooze on these patches! You can wake your zombies up or make them go to sleep by tapping on the patch.


 Q: What is a Zombie Camera?


 A Zombie Camera, once placed on your farm, can be used to take pictures. Tap on the Zombie Camera and he'll take a quick snapshot of whatever your view is on the device. After taking the picture, you'll be given the options to either send it to an e-mail address or to post it on your Facebook page (internet connection required).


 Q: Will I still get experience points from plowing if I buy a Plowing Monolith?


 No, but planting will give you double experience.


 Q: What's good about having friends?


 When you add someone to your friends list in-game, you can visit their farm, play tag with their zombies, and send them free gifts.  With all that, who wouldn't want to have friends in Zombie Farm!?


 Q: Will there be more items in the market?


 Yes, we periodically will come up with updates which will include new additions to the market.


 Q: I bought/planted too much stuff, now my farmer is broke!


 You can always sell what you have to make back some gold. Zombies sell for especially high prices. You can also trade brains for gold in the market if you have any. If you have absolutely no way to get gold back, you can always create a new Playforge account and start over.  


 Q: Zombie Farm is good! I want to tell you how much I like it!


 That's great! Don't forget to rate us in the App Store to let other people know how much you like it.  You can also like us on Facebook and post on our discussion board.


 Q: Something broke on Zombie Farm! Now I am sad =(


 Don't be sad! Go to our Zombie Farm support forum by visiting support.theplayforge.com, and post your problem there :)


 Q: Wouldn't it be cool if Zombie Farm had...


 Whoa hold on there! Go to our Facebook page first and check out our discussion board to tell us about it. You can join one of the many suggestion threads or start your own. We do read the boards regularly.


 Q: Where can I find Zombie Farm's Facebook page?


 Just go to facebook.com/ZombieFarm, and join in the discussion today!

 You can find more zombie jokes as well as news updates, brain giveaways, and much more by following @theplayforge on Twitter!
